body:
## Design for the B2B Buyer Who Wants to Research Alone

Modern B2B software buying is increasingly self-directed. That changes what a landing page needs to do. The page cannot assume that every serious buyer wants to book a call before seeing meaningful evidence. At the same time, self-service only works when buyers can independently answer the questions that create hesitation.

### Bring peer evidence into the journey

G2's 2024 Buyer Behavior Report surveyed 1,940 B2B decision-makers across North America, EMEA, and APAC. It found that public product-review websites were the most consulted information source for 31% of buyers, up from 23% in 2023. G2 also reported that respondents considered independent review sites more valuable than analyst firms at every buying stage it measured. (Sell G2)

For a SaaS landing page, that suggests making peer validation easy to reach rather than relying entirely on vendor-owned proof. A third-party review excerpt can support a specific claim. An aggregate rating can provide a quick signal. A community quote can add experience-level detail. A verified reviewer profile can help buyers understand who is speaking. These are different ways to serve the same need: evidence that does not originate solely with the seller.

### Make security evidence self-service

Enterprise software buyers frequently need information that is more detailed than a compliance logo. G2 found that 81% of its 2024 respondents considered a vendor's history of security breaches or incidents when evaluating software, while 48% said they had closed a purchase without the chosen vendor completing a security or privacy assessment. (Sell G2) The report also found that 35% of buyers were unaware of security and privacy assessment processes and tools available to them, and it recommended leading with security credentials and detailed assessment guides. (Sell G2)

That creates several viable landing-page patterns. A Trust Center can be a primary navigation destination. Certification badges can link to verification details. A downloadable security questionnaire can support procurement. A security overview can sit directly beside an enterprise CTA. The design choice should follow how formal the buying process is.

### Offer independence without removing the human path

Gartner reported that 75% of B2B buyers preferred a rep-free purchase experience, while buyers using self-service digital commerce were 1.65 times more likely to experience purchase regret than those using traditional sales channels. (Gartner) This is a useful tension rather than a contradiction. Buyers want independence, but independence creates a need for better evidence.

A strong landing page can therefore offer a self-guided product tour, transparent pricing and packaging, technical documentation, or a trial/sandbox, while also providing an optional route to sales. The human path becomes a support mechanism rather than a prerequisite. The research does not demand one CTA pattern; it supports designing the page so buyers can choose the level of interaction they need.
